name: Sub setting group
summary: The dependent (child) settings wrapper — indents a cluster of sub-settings under one parent toggle with a tighter gap, spacing only (no border, no card).
highlights: Indents sub-settings under one parent toggle, 16px below it
Spacing only: no border, no card
lead: ONE custom element — <aha-sub-setting-group> — for the settings-panel case where turning one setting on reveals a cluster of dependent sub-settings. It gives them the nesting treatment with SPACING only: 16px below its parent (tighter than the 24 between siblings, so the child reads as "belongs to" its parent) and a 24px indent — NO left border, NO card. The host owns visibility: the author adds `hidden` when the parent is off (`:host([hidden]){display:none}`); the component just does the nesting. Labels inside it are regular 400 in secondary text (--aha-text-secondary) via the --aha-setting-label-color custom property — the indent + tighter gap are the primary signal. role="group". Shadow-DOM CSS, themed only by --aha-* tokens → byte-identical in React and Vue. Zero drift.
codeNote: Same element, same shadow-DOM CSS → identical render. React (< 19) consumes it via a thin wrapper; Vue binds the custom element natively. Defined once in @ahaslides-product/design.

opinion.note: Use this only for genuinely dependent settings — ones that are meaningless until a parent is on. Keep the parent row and its sub-group inside the same setting group. Hide (not disable) the sub-settings when the parent is off, so the panel doesn't fill with dead controls. Never draw a left rail or box around the nest — the 24px indent + the 16px bind are the whole signal.

conformance.$about: Measured by qa.mjs against the RENDERED UI (getComputedStyle via headless CDP). Leaf = ONE shared element, single render. The probe is a sub-group nested under a parent row inside a setting group. Measures ≥4 props incl colours (nested text + nested label) + px (padding-left 24, margin-top -8 = 16 below the parent).
